key_insight: A differentiable overlapping Schwarz solver couples near-wall and bulk transport, enabling inverse modeling of thin boundary layers with agentic AI-assisted optimization.
engineering_relevance: The framework reduces mesh-resolution demands for high-Péclet-number transport while enforcing governing equations and boundary conditions as hard constraints.
method: Use perturbation theory to separate near-wall and bulk equations, then discretize both with finite elements.
Couple overlapping domains through differentiable Schwarz iterations that enforce interface continuity.
Use adjoint sensitivities with LLM-driven parameter updates or an agent that stages optimization and expands a functional basis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower computational cost than a single-domain formulation and the greatest agentic AI advantage for functional-basis unknowns, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The reported agentic advantage depends on the unknown representation, so benefits for high-dimensional nodal fields should not be assumed.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
